title: In emergencies the Operational Facilitator may compress the Root Edit timeline and may withhold the public announcement
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 grants a timeline override: "In an Urgent or Emergency Situation, as defined by the Sky Core Atlas in A.1.9.1.1, the Operational Facilitator may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above."

Two containment devices are attached. The trigger condition is defined *elsewhere and upward* — in the Core Atlas, not in the Skybase Artifact — so the Agent cannot widen its own emergency conditions through a Root Edit. And disclosure is expected: the Facilitator "should announce the decision to deploy the emergency Root Edit protocol and provide their reasoning via a public Sky Forum post."

But the disclosure obligation is doubly softened: it applies only "where feasible," and is excused "unless doing so would endanger Skybase or its users." That carve-out is defensible — announcing an emergency fix can advertise the vulnerability it fixes — yet it means the emergency path can in principle run without contemporaneous public notice, and the judgment about danger belongs to the same role that invoked the emergency.

What is *not* waived matters as much as what is. The provision compresses the timeline only; it does not exempt the edit from the alignment review or the Artifact Edit Restrictions, so an emergency Root Edit still cannot violate the Core Atlas.
description: Acceleration is keyed to the Core Atlas definition of Urgent and Emergency Situations; disclosure is owed only 'where feasible' and is excused when it would endanger Skybase or its users.
